text: I got the offer but honestly the interview was mostly questions I had seen before. I think I just got a lucky draw on the panel, another candidate with the same prep would have done better.
Standup again today. Everyone rattles off what they shipped and I say I'm still reading the codebase. Three weeks in. They must be wondering when someone is going to notice they hired wrong.
My manager said my design doc was the clearest one she'd read this quarter. I mean it was a small doc and she is nice to everyone, so.

Spent the whole weekend rehearsing a fifteen minute demo. I know it's too much. But if I get one question wrong in front of the staff engineers that's the moment they figure out I don't actually understand the system.
Exhausted. Deploy broke at 11pm, rolled it back, went to bed at 3. I am so tired of this on-call rotation and I don't think the schedule is sustainable for anyone on the team.
Really down today. Nothing specific happened, I just feel flat and can't get interested in anything, including things I normally like.
Finally fixed the race condition that had been open for a month. Took two days of reading traces and I'm genuinely proud of the fix.
Presented at the team meeting and it went fine, people asked good questions. Afterwards I kept replaying the one thing I stumbled on. I keep waiting for someone to ask the question I can't answer.
Everyone in my cohort seems to already know Kubernetes and system design and I'm still googling git commands. I don't know how they all got so far ahead.
Got promoted. My skip level said it was overdue. But the timing was just right, the team grew and they needed someone at that level, so it was more about headcount than about me.
Wrote 400 lines of tests for a 40 line change because I could not stand the idea of a reviewer finding a case I missed. Took the whole day. Nobody asked for that.
Coffee with Priya was lovely, we talked about her new apartment and the hiking trip in October. First time in weeks I haven't thought about work on a Saturday.
